title: Localised Adaptive Spatial-Temporal Graph Neural Network

problem.claim: It is unclear whether and to what extent adaptive spatial-temporal graph neural networks can be localised.

contributions.claim: The authors propose Adaptive Graph Sparsification, an algorithm for sparsifying spatial graph adjacency matrices to localise adaptive spatial-temporal graph neural networks.
The study evaluates Adaptive Graph Sparsification on two adaptive spatial-temporal graph neural network architectures and nine spatial-temporal datasets.
The proposed localisation approach is presented as having potential to reduce computation overhead on large-scale spatial-temporal data and enable distributed deployment.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The spatial graphs were sparsified by over 99.5% without a decline in test accuracy.
Fully localised, graph-less and purely temporal models showed no accuracy drop on the majority of tested datasets, with minor deterioration on the remaining datasets.
Reinitialising and retraining partially or fully localised models on the same data produced a considerable and consistent accuracy drop.

narrative_sequence.summary: Spatial-temporal graph models are used to model spatial and temporal dependencies.
The work investigates whether and to what extent adaptive spatial-temporal graph neural networks can be localised.
Localisation is pursued by sparsifying spatial graph adjacency matrices with Adaptive Graph Sparsification.
The approach is applied to two architectures and nine spatial-temporal datasets, with substantial sparsification and limited inference accuracy deterioration reported.
The observations suggest that spatial information may be redundant for inference but important for effective training.

source_observation.claim: Spatial graphs can reportedly be sparsified by over 99.5% without declining test accuracy, and full localisation causes no accuracy drop on most tested datasets.

interpretation.claim: For the tested data, spatial dependencies may largely duplicate information available through temporal dependencies during inference.

application.claim: When deploying spatial-temporal models, test whether aggressive spatial sparsification or graph removal can reduce computation while preserving inference accuracy.

exception.claim: Spatial dependencies may remain important during training, since reinitialisation and retraining after localisation caused a considerable and consistent accuracy drop.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the two evaluated architectures or nine datasets.
The abstract does not provide experimental settings, baselines, statistical variation, or computational measurements.
